chunks.text: Operating Systems - Process Scheduling Notes Introduction: Process scheduling is a fundamental OS function that decides which process runs at a given time. Types of Scheduling: Long-term, Short-term, and Medium-term scheduling. Scheduling Algorithms: FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority Scheduling. FCFS: First Come First Serve, simple but can cause long waiting times. SJF: Shortest Job First, optimal but hard to predict burst time. Round Robin: Time-sharing system using time quantum. Priority Scheduling: Processes are scheduled based on priority. Key Concepts: Waiting time, Turnaround time, Response time. Conclusion: Efficient scheduling improves CPU utilization and system performance.
